rationale: The source gives the standard field axioms; the item repackages them as two abelian-group structures with distributivity and the explicit convention 0 != 1. The wording and presentation differ but the quantified structure is the same; no proof is applicable.

The source defines the same compatible total ordering on a field. The item uses the equivalent positive-cone convention and derives < from membership in the cone, so this is a semantic rather than verbatim match; no proof is applicable.
The university notes give the same piecewise definition on an ordered field, including the x >= 0 and x < 0 branches. No proof is applicable.

The source lists cofinality of the canonical naturals as an equivalent definition of an Archimedean ordered field. The item chooses that equivalent formulation and spells out n times the unit; no proof is applicable.
The notes define a complete ordered field by the same least-upper-bound condition for every nonempty bounded-above subset. No proof is applicable.

The source gives the standard unital field-homomorphism definition and injectivity consequence. The item restates the three preservation identities and separately names embeddings and isomorphisms; no proof is applicable.
The notes use the same notion of a bijective field homomorphism preserving the order in both directions. No proof is applicable.
The source states uniqueness of additive and multiplicative identities and inverses in a field. The proof is a locally expanded abelian-group calculation following the standard argument.
The source states that zero times any field element is zero. The proof adapts the standard distributivity-and-cancellation calculation into numbered steps.
The source states the same rules a(-b)=-(ab), (-a)b=-(ab), and (-a)(-b)=ab in an ordered/field setting. The proof expands the usual distributivity argument.
The source explicitly records (-1)(-1)=1. The supplied two-step proof is a local specialization of the preceding sign lemma rather than a sourced proof adaptation.
The source states that every field is an integral domain, hence has no zero divisors. The proof follows the standard multiplication-by-an-inverse argument in expanded form.
The source gives cancellation by a nonzero field element. The proof is the standard inverse calculation, resegmented into the local proof format.

The source states translation invariance of an ordered-field order. The item combines that result with the immediate sum-of-two-strict-inequalities consequence; its proof is a local positive-cone derivation.

The source gives the same positive- and negative-factor order laws. The item aggregates product-sign cases and both biconditional cancellation forms; the proof is locally assembled from the cone axioms.
The university notes state that every nonzero square in an ordered field is positive. The proof follows the standard trichotomy split and is locally expanded.
The source explicitly states 0 < 1 in every ordered field. The local proof derives it as the direct square-of-one corollary rather than following a sourced proof.

The source states positivity of inverses and reversal of order under reciprocation for positive elements. The item packages both forms together and the proof adapts the standard positive-product argument.

The textbook theorem contains the same absolute-value positivity, zero, product, symmetry, bound, and interval characterizations. The item consolidates those clauses and adapts the source's case analysis.
The textbook states the triangle inequality for every ordered field in the same form. The proof follows its two-sided-bound argument with local citation detail.
The textbook states the same reverse triangle inequality. The proof adapts the standard two applications of the triangle inequality.

The three equivalences are standard ordered-field consequences of b^2-a^2=(b-a)(b+a) and |x|^2=x^2, but no reputable source with the complete compound statement surfaced after targeted searches. The formulation is recognizable established mathematics rather than an invented claim; Alpha independently concurred from the current statement and local derivation at A6.

The source gives reciprocal positivity and order reversal on positive elements. The item normalizes these facts around the threshold 1 and adds the equality case; the proof adapts the standard inverse-order calculation.
The source records the ordered-field product sign rules and absence of zero divisors. The item combines them into three biconditionals; its exhaustive proof is locally composed.

The textbook develops ordered-field multiplication inequalities, including the strict positive four-variable form; the item adds the nonstrict boundary version. The proof is a local two-stage comparison and case split.

The equivalence 0<ab<b iff 0<a<1 for b>0 is a standard one-line ordered-field cancellation fact, but no reputable source with this exact formulation surfaced after targeted searches. It is recoverable established knowledge, not a novel statement; Alpha independently concurred from the current statement and local derivation at A6.

The source constructs the canonical natural elements 1, 1+1, and so on inside a field. The item recasts this as the recursively defined map from N including 0 and states the notation explicitly; no proof is applicable.

The source develops the canonical naturals and their arithmetic in an ordered field. The item combines positivity, strict increase, injectivity, addition, and multiplication into one induction lemma; the proof is locally assembled.
The university notes state that every complete ordered field is Archimedean in the same canonical-natural cofinality form. The proof adapts the standard supremum-of-the-naturals contradiction.

The source lists the cofinal-natural and reciprocal/infimum formulations as equivalent Archimedean properties. The item specializes the reciprocal form to a complete ordered field and the proof expands the inversion step.

The notes give the unique order-preserving homomorphism Q into any ordered field with the same integer and fraction formulas. The item states the field-homomorphism uniqueness, injectivity, and ordered-subfield conclusions explicitly; the proof adapts that construction.
The university notes state exactly that Q is dense in any Archimedean ordered field. The proof follows the standard scale-to-an-integer argument with the local canonical embedding made explicit.

The source proves existence and uniqueness of nonnegative square roots in a complete ordered field. The item adds the equivalent characterization of positive elements as nonzero squares; its supremum proof is adapted from the standard source argument.

The source proves uniqueness of the canonical homomorphism from Q to an ordered field. The item expresses the resulting naturality equation for an arbitrary field homomorphism between ordered fields; the proof adapts the standard integer-and-fraction calculation.

The claim is the standard consequence that positives in a complete ordered field are nonzero squares and field homomorphisms preserve nonzero squares, but no reputable source with this domain-and-codomain formulation surfaced after targeted searches. It is established mathematics with a local proof, not an invented bridge; Alpha independently concurred from the current statement and local derivation at A6.
The source states that any two complete ordered fields are uniquely order-isomorphic. The proof adapts the standard rational-cut construction and expands preservation, surjectivity, and uniqueness.
The construction notes state that the Cauchy-sequence real field is Archimedean. The proof adapts the rational-approximation argument to the repository's constant-sequence notation.

The Purdue notes construct the Cauchy-sequence reals as a complete ordered field, which is exactly the least-upper-bound conclusion here. The ETSU proof gives the nested-bisection argument adapted in the supplied proof; two of its local limit citations are imprecise and are recorded separately as an A2 defect.

The sources state that the Cauchy and Dedekind constructions are classically isomorphic and that complete ordered-field models are uniquely isomorphic. The item combines these into a single preservation-rich formulation; its proof is a local application of the repository uniqueness theorem.

The sources give the unique positive square root of 2 in a complete ordered field and the irrationality of sqrt(2). The example combines those standard results with the canonical rational embedding; its proof is locally composed.
The source gives the same conjugation homomorphism on Q(sqrt(2)) as a field homomorphism that is not order-preserving. The verification expands closure, inverses, and the sign reversal.

The source gives the same eventually-positive ordering of a rational-function field and the element exceeding every natural. The verification adapts the usual leading-term/sign argument; its overbroad local citation is recorded separately as an A2 defect.

This is a bespoke pedagogical false statement, not an asserted established theorem. Its falsity is directly verified by the cited uniqueness theorem: applying that theorem to the alleged pair immediately supplies the forbidden isomorphism.
